title: A perfectly symmetric world, broken by rounding error
view: whole 256^2 world, 2 px per cell; right panel max(|A - rot90 A|, |A - A^T|) per cell, log10, viridis from -16 to 0 (values below 1e-16, including exact zeros, shown as -16)
measured: max asymmetry 0 at t = 0, about 2e-13 at 5 tu, 3e-10 at 15 tu, 2e-5 at 25 tu, 1 by 40 tu (asymmetry.csv; growth roughly 30x per 5 tu while the colony grows)
caveats: The rule and the initial state are exactly symmetric, so in exact arithmetic the world stays symmetric. The symmetry is broken by floating-point rounding in the FFT convolution (float64, numpy pocketfft) and then amplified. Another FFT library or summation order would break it differently.
One seed; in a 24-run pilot of D4 soups (seeds 0-11 at amplitudes 0.3 and 0.35), 8 filled the world and 16 died out, and every survivor was fully asymmetric (max difference 1) by 100 tu.
The world-filling lattice is the same kind of state as G010's filled soups (C056).

runs.initial_state: d4_soup(seed=4): 40x40 uniform [0, 0.3) block (numpy default_rng(4)), symmetrised across the diagonal and mirrored into an 80x80 patch with all 8 square symmetries, centred on zero 256^2

render.colormap: matplotlib inferno, A in [0,1] mapped linearly, nearest-neighbour
